name: Body sensors
plain: Asks to read heart rate and similar body sensor data while the app is in use.
meaning: Heart rate and related vitals reveal fitness, stress and health conditions. Android 16 replaces this permission with granular health permissions for apps targeting 36.

android.permission: BODY_SENSORS (replaced by android.permissions.health.* for apps targeting 36)
android.prompt_ui: Allow or Don't allow (While using the app, Only this time on Android 11+ for foreground sensors)
android.revocation: Settings > Apps > Permissions > Body sensors (or Health Connect permissions on 16)
android.store_policy: Play: health apps declaration for Health Connect data
android.note: Android 16 (API 36): apps targeting 36 must use granular health permissions; a privacy-policy rationale activity is required or the permission is revoked.

ios.prompt_ui: Per data type read and write toggles in the Health sheet
ios.persistence: Until revoked; read denial looks like no data
ios.revocation: Health app > Sharing > Apps; Settings > Privacy > Health
ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.3: health data may not be used for advertising or sold
ios.note: Apps cannot tell if read access was denied or the user has no data.

data.update: about 1 sample per second to a few per minute, device dependent

limits.headline: Can see your heart rate and similar body signals while the app is open
limits.user_action: You tap Start workout or Measure heart rate and then Allow
can: See live heart rate from the phone or a connected watch while the app is open
Choose While using the app or Only this time on Android 11 and newer
Ask for per type access in the Health sheet on iPhone
Show your readings during a workout
cannot: See your heart rate when the app is closed, without the extra background permission
Use the old body sensors permission in apps aimed at Android 16; granular health permissions replace it
Tell on iPhone if you denied access; it just looks like no data
Keep going if you turn it off in Settings
limits.differs: Android 16 replaces this with finer health permissions and a privacy policy step. iPhone uses the Health sheet with per type switches.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app read your heart rate and similar body readings while you use it.

marketing.name: Health Connect
marketing.pitch: Developer pitch: one place for health and fitness data with user control over which apps can read or write it.

story.for_you: A pop up asks to access body sensors. If you allow it, the app can read your heart rate and similar vitals while you use it. It can show stress or health problems, so say yes only for a good reason.
story.for_makers: Fitness and wellness apps use it to show live heart rate and zones. Android 16 replaces this old permission with narrower health permissions for apps that target it.

use_cases.example: A running app shows live heart rate zones from your watch during a workout.
A meditation app reads heart rate to show if you calm down.
A fitness game speeds up or slows down based on your heart rate.
A watch companion app shows today's resting heart rate.
A coaching app suggests rest when your heart rate stays high.
An ad firm could infer stress or health conditions if heart data leaked.
A driver safety app watches heart rate for signs of drowsiness.

risks: Data can be sold or leaked
story.android_note: Uses the BODY_SENSORS permission, replaced by granular health permissions on Android 16.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps read heart rate through HealthKit permissions, per data type.

technical_bounds: Android 16 binds sensors to Health Connect permission model
Apple review blocks ads from health data

abuse: Health inference for insurance or ads

history.change: Apps targeting 36 move from BODY_SENSORS to granular health permissions shared with Health Connect
